_Story by Tom Perkins_

ANN ARBOR, Mich.--A judge has thrown out felony embezzlement and false
pretense charges against a pro-Palestinian University of Michigan student that
alleged she used university funds to illegally purchase laptops for a student
club.

Organizers with the Graduate Employees' Organization (GEO) here
[say](https://www.geo3550.org/2026/08/14/geo-president-charges-dismissed/) the
charges, which a judge dismissed on August 7, are yet another example of U-M
trying to shut down criticism of Israel over its genocide in Gaza. The
student, Hiab Teshome, is also a graduate student union leader in tense
contract negotiations with the school. The union has organized against
university support for Israel's genocide, and pro-Palestinian advocates told
Drop Site that the case against Teshome was a "political prosecution."

The investigation and warrant requests were led by Ryan Cavanaugh, a
University of Michigan Police Department sergeant who faces allegations in two
federal lawsuits that he violated a range of students' constitutional rights
throughout the school's multiyear crackdown.

The student and a co-defendant, whose case was also dismissed, were involved
with organizing a May 2024 encampment, and are organizing on behalf of the
protesters that Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel and the Trump DOJ [are
targeting](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/university-michigan-palestine-
protests-federal-indictments-nessel-sayed). GEO says Cavanaugh's actions are
part of an ongoing harassment campaign he is waging against pro-Palestinian
students.

Eli Savit, a progressive Jewish prosecutor in Ann Arbor who's running for
state attorney general to replace the term-limited Nessel, brought the
charges. Nessel has led the state and U-M's legal campaign against pro-
Palestinain students in recent years, and Savit beat a pro-Israel-donor-backed
opponent in the Democratic nomination. He in part won because the progressive
base views him as a break from Nessel and the political establishment's
unpopular prosecutions and positions on Israel.

Teshome was a co-signer on the laptop purchases for the Blue Talks medical
student club, but did not actually make the purchase, and never possessed the
devices. Another member of the club used the laptop and was reimbursed for it.

The prosecutor's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment,
but in its case claimed the student should not have been reimbursed because,
it alleged, the club was defunct, and Teshome was in part responsible because
she co-signed the purchase. Organizers say the club was not defunct.

The purchase was approved by U-M, and the school's auditors initially found a
discrepancy, but did not flag any wrongdoing, advocates say. The U-M Central
Student Government (CSG), which handles financial discrepancies with student
clubs, also did not find wrongdoing.

Multiple sources with knowledge of the investigation said Cavanaugh's warrant
requests were highly unusual because he bypassed administrative channels to
resolve the issue.

"GEO will not stand for any attempts by the University of Michigan and its
collaborators in the legal system to repress Palestine solidarity or labor
organizing," the group said in a statement.
